delivered.outbound_channel: business-channel.ts now owns BOTH directions: the Runner's inbound waiters and its outbound callbacks (fact, payload-read, native-write-intent), all scoped to the lease generation that created them
delivered.routes: GET /v1/channel/next hands the lease the next callback, POST /v1/channel/reply routes one reply to the request it names. Both sit behind the existing bearer auth; the producer is the authenticated one and the lease id only scopes waiter ownership, so it grants nothing

item4_B11_ackPoints.finding: on the short-lived codex-fake lane the second command resolved as successful while the receiver log recorded ZERO receptions: a resolved bridge call is not proof of reception. item4_B11_ackPoints.labelling: the second command is a deliver, which uses the SAME admission and receipt path as the answer; it is not relabelled as an answer. The answer is counted separately on the product lane by b27-ack-windows.

item4_singleChain.case: B27-CHAIN-ONE-BINDING-ACROSS-KILL - three coordinator PIDs, one deliberate SIGKILL in the middle, saw ONE attempt at ONE epoch with the same original fact ids; the re-fed begin was RECEIVED a second time but ADMITTED only once (duplicate_begin)
item4_singleChain.distinction: reception count and admission count are different facts and are reported separately instead of conflated: the frame reaching the receiver is not the same as the command being executed twice

chainCallbackOrdering.finding: the Runner asks its bound lease for outbound callbacks ONLY while a lease is bound. A coordinator that attaches after the facts have already flowed cannot serve them, because those facts were acknowledged over stdio at the moment they were raised. Serving the three callbacks inside the SAME chain as the SIGKILL therefore requires the lease to bind BEFORE begin.
chainCallbackOrdering.consequence: the callback servicing is observed on b27-dual-client (controlled endpoint) and b27-dual-live (real child), and the kill chain on b27-sigkill; they are not yet one run, and this is stated rather than merged
chainCallbackOrdering.nextStep: bind a serving lease before begin on the live lane, let it serve the fact callbacks, SIGKILL it mid-flight, and let the successor lease finish the same attempt - one run, one attempt, one epoch

item4_singleChainRun.orderingRuleApplied: the serving lease binds BEFORE begin, which is what makes the Runner route its callbacks to the channel instead of stdio
